sections.h2: Where does the Manitowoc County Register of Deeds record deeds?
sections.html:
The Manitowoc County Register of Deeds sits in the county courthouse at 1010 S 8th Street, 1st Floor, Room 107, Manitowoc, WI 54220. Every deed, mortgage and satisfaction on a Manitowoc County house is recorded there, and the office keeps the permanent index of those records.

Hours on the county page are Monday 8:30 to 5:00 and Tuesday through Friday 8:30 to 4:30. The real estate page adds that documents are recorded daily from 8:30 AM to 4:00 PM, so plan to arrive well before 4:00 PM. The main phone number is 920-683-4660.

Staff here cannot draft a deed or give legal advice. If your sale involves an inherited house, a land contract or a title problem, a Wisconsin attorney or the title company handling the closing should prepare the paperwork before it reaches the counter.

sections.h2: What is Manitowoc County like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Manitowoc County covers 1,494 square miles on the Lake Michigan shore, but only 589 of those square miles are land. The other 905 square miles (61 percent) are water. The county was created in 1836 and organized in 1848, and the city of Manitowoc is the county seat. Since 2021 much of the northern half of the Wisconsin Shipwreck Coast National Marine Sanctuary has lain off its coast.

The Census Bureau counted 81,359 residents in 2020 and estimated 81,710 for July 2025, a gain of about 0.4 percent. About 24.8 percent of residents are 65 or older, a share that matters when a family sells a parent's house.

  • Housing units: 38,298 (July 2025 estimate).
  • Owner-occupied rate: 77.1 percent (2020 to 2024).
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $186,900.
  • Median gross rent: $797 a month.
  • Median household income: $69,148.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 152.

With a median home value under $190,000, the $30 recording fee and the transfer fee on a typical Manitowoc County sale are small next to repair and carrying costs. The paperwork rules are the same for a $90,000 house as for a $400,000 one.

sections.h2: How much does it cost to record a deed in Manitowoc County?
sections.html:
Recording one deed costs $30 under Wis. Stat. 59.43(2)(ag), and the fee is due in advance. Copies cost $2 for the first page and $1 for each page after that, plus $1 to certify a copy. These base amounts are set by state law, so they apply in every Wisconsin county.

ItemAmountSource
Recording a deed or mortgage$30 per documentWis. Stat. 59.43(2)(ag)
Copy of a recorded document$2 first page, $1 each added pageWis. Stat. 59.43(2)(b)
Certifying a copy$1 extraWis. Stat. 59.43(2)(b)
Subdivision or condominium plat$50Wis. Stat. 59.43(2)(h)
State real estate transfer fee30 cents per $100 of valueWis. Stat. 77.22(1)

The county posts a separate fee schedule link on its real estate page. Ask the Register of Deeds for the current office schedule if you need anything beyond these statutory items, such as search or special handling charges.

sections.h2: How does the Wisconsin transfer fee work on a Manitowoc County sale?
sections.html:
The seller (the grantor) owes a transfer fee of 30 cents for each $100 of value, or fraction of $100, under Wis. Stat. 77.22. On a $186,900 sale, roughly the county median home value, that comes to about $561. The Register of Deeds collects it when the deed is submitted and writes the amount on the face of the deed.

Twenty percent of the fee stays with the county and the rest goes to the state, according to Wis. Stat. 77.24. The office does not check whether your stated price is correct. Section 77.22 says the register has no duty to determine the true value or to test an exemption claim, so the return you sign carries your own statement under the law.

Some conveyances owe no fee. Section 77.25 lists exemptions such as these:

  • A transfer by will, descent or survivorship.
  • A transfer between parent and child, stepparent and stepchild, or grandparent and grandchild for nominal or no consideration.
  • A transfer of real estate worth $1,000 or less.
  • A deed under foreclosure, or in lieu of foreclosure, to the mortgage holder or land contract seller.
  • A transfer on a sale for delinquent taxes or assessments.

When a deed is exempt, the reason must be stated on its face by citing the right subsection of 77.25.

sections.h2: What must a deed include before Manitowoc County will record it?
sections.html:
The office may refuse a document that does not substantially follow the standard format in Wis. Stat. 59.43(2m). The statute asks for the following:

  • A clear document title placed between 0.5 inch and 6 inches from the top of page one.
  • A blank 3 inch by 3 inch space in the upper right corner of the first page for the recording stamp.
  • Return information on page one, unless the document is recorded electronically.
  • White paper of at least 20 pound weight, 8.5 inches wide and 11 or 14 inches long.
  • Black, blue or red ink, with pages not hinged or joined along the top or sides.
  • The name of the person or agency that drafted the document.
  • Clearly written or typed names for the grantor, grantee and any notary.

A document that contains an individual's Social Security number cannot be recorded under subsection (1m). Strip any such number before you submit the deed. If a group of documents is presented as one transaction and one of them fails the format rules, the register may send the whole set back unrecorded.

sections.h2: Can a deed be recorded electronically in Manitowoc County?
sections.html:
Yes. The Manitowoc County real estate page lists four e-recording providers and says each has a sign-up process: Simplifile at 713-210-4323, Hopdox at 385-501-5103, Indecomm at 651-765-6400 and EPN at 888-325-3365. If a title company or closing attorney handles your sale, ask whether it will submit the deed through one of these providers.

Every deed also needs a Wisconsin Electronic Real Estate Transfer Return (ERETR). The county page tells filers to save the return before pressing submit and to print the receipt, because the receipt must travel with the original deed when it is recorded at the office. Leave the page without printing it and you have to file the return again.

sections.h2: How can an owner guard against deed fraud in Manitowoc County?
sections.html:
Sign up for the free notification service the Register of Deeds offers. It tells you when a document is recorded against your name or property so you can confirm it is genuine. The county describes real estate fraud as rare in Wisconsin, and the alert costs nothing and takes one call to 920-683-4660.

The service is especially useful for owners who live out of the area, hold an inherited house that sits empty, or are waiting on a sale to close. Once your own deed is recorded, you can use the same alert to watch for anything filed afterward.

faqs.q: What is the address of the Manitowoc County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: It is in the Manitowoc County Courthouse at 1010 S 8th Street, 1st Floor, Room 107, Manitowoc, WI 54220. The phone number is 920-683-4660. Hours are Monday 8:30 to 5:00 and Tuesday through Friday 8:30 to 4:30, and documents are recorded daily from 8:30 AM to 4:00 PM.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Manitowoc County?
faqs.a: The statutory recording fee is $30 per document, payable in advance under Wis. Stat. 59.43(2)(ag). Add the state transfer fee of 30 cents per $100 of value if the sale is not exempt. Copies are $2 for the first page and $1 for each added page, with $1 more to certify.

faqs.q: Do I need to file anything with the state before the deed is recorded?
faqs.a: Yes. File a Wisconsin Electronic Real Estate Transfer Return, then print the receipt. The Manitowoc County page says the receipt must accompany the original deed when you record at the Register of Deeds. Only conveyances exempt under Wis. Stat. 77.25(1) or (10m) skip the return.

faqs.q: Does a transfer of an inherited house owe the transfer fee?
faqs.a: Usually not. A conveyance by will, descent or survivorship is exempt under Wis. Stat. 77.25(11). A later sale of the inherited house to a buyer is a different conveyance and carries the fee based on the price. Ask the Register of Deeds or a Wisconsin attorney how to document the first transfer.

faqs.q: Can I record a deed in Manitowoc County by e-recording?
faqs.a: Yes. The county lists Simplifile, Hopdox, Indecomm and EPN as e-recording providers, each with its own sign-up phone number. Ask your title company or closing attorney whether it will submit the deed through one of them.
